Sam / team —

Thanks for the notes. I'm attaching a short markdown snippet for the KV-cache warm-up + a slightly updated test matrix (rls-loadtest-plan-v1 -> rls-loadtest-plan-v2). Highlights:

- Sequence profiling assumptions: 80% tokens <= 64, 15% between 65-256, 5% >256. If your real distribution differs, tell us and we'll re-calc expected per-token latency.
- Batching strategy: continuous smart batching with a 8-token soft cutoff and 40ms max coalescing window for steady-state.
- Target steady-state: 1,400 QPS per replica across 3 replicas (4-node pool) for the baseline run.
- Warm-up: 10min progressive ramp to full QPS with prefix priming for popular prompt families.
- Disruption plan: if tail latency > p95 target, we'll automatically reduce max batch size and fail over to a quantized 8-bit variant; ops runbook will open an incident and revert to baseline once p95 < target for 10min.

Proposed concrete slot to confirm based on Alex's note: Tue Apr 6, 15:30–16:45 PDT (90m to give time for handoffs). If that works for PlutoApps we'll send the calendar invite.

Attachments: kv-cache-runbook.md, rls-loadtest-plan-v2.pdf

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Performance
Redwood Inference
